title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Seller's Release of Liability on an Assumed Loan
content:
A veteran selling a home to a buyer who assumes the VA Home Loan Guaranty loan may ask, in the veteran's own name, to be released from personal liability on that loan. The release records the guaranty that stays in force on the loan for the assuming buyer.

## When the figure is fixed

The guaranty that stays in force on an assumed loan is fixed only after the loan record shows the loan current again, with every reported default cured by a partial claim entry in its money transactions.

Put another way: while the loan record shows a reported default that no partial claim entry in the loan's money transactions has cured, the guaranty that stays in force is not fixed.

## What the release does

The release marks the loan as released by assumption, records that the veteran is released from liability with today's date as the release date, and records the guaranty that stays in force on the loan for the assuming buyer at the figure the representative has told the veteran. The loan record then shows the seller released from liability on the assumption.

## Invocation

The release is requested with the veteran's own tool `request_release_of_liability_741ed869`. The representative unlocks it for the veteran (`unlock_user_discoverable_tool`) and hands it over; the customer themselves, the veteran as the seller, personally signs the request by running it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `loan_id` | The reference number of the VA home loan record being assumed, as given to the veteran by the representative from the loan lookup | Identifier |
| `guaranty_amount` | The guaranty that stays in force on the loan after the release | USD, a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed |

### Return

On success the veteran receives a receipt with `loan_id` (the loan released), `loan_status` (always `released_by_assumption`), `release_of_liability` (always True), `release_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD) and `guaranty_amount` (USD, 2 decimal places, the guaranty recorded as in force). No other outcome is defined.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A veteran who runs the tool with the reference of the assumed loan and `guaranty_amount` 54,000.00 receives a receipt showing `loan_status` `released_by_assumption`, `release_of_liability` True, today's `release_date` and `guaranty_amount` 54,000.00.
